title: Packaging Playbook: Inference Feature Decision Worksheet
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook captures a repeatable decision process for how new inference-facing features should be packaged across Redwood delivery surfaces (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It is intended for product managers, pricing, runtime engineers, and solutions teams so that packaging choices are consistent, measurable, and operationally-sound.

Quick summary

- Purpose: determine a single recommended packaging configuration for a feature and record tradeoffs, telemetries, rollout constraints, and pricing mappings.
- Scope: new inference features (generation modes, hybrid streaming/batch, adaptive quantization, cache coordination) and significant packaging changes to existing features.
- Owners: Product (feature lead), Pricing, Eng (runtime/product), SRE/Ops, Solutions.

Goals and acceptance metrics

- Deliver a packaging decision within 10 business days after PRD approval.
- Produce concrete quantitative estimates: median per-token cost delta, p95 latency delta, and GPU-hour impact.
- Canary acceptance: error-rate regression <= 3% absolute, p95 latency within SLO target for canary tenants.

Required decision inputs

1) Product: PRD link, target personas, example traffic shapes, required fidelity modes.
2) Pricing/Economics: per-route simulated cost, suggested SKU/credit mapping, expected revenue impact.
3) Runtime: supported quantization/variants, memory footprint, throughput & batching profile.
4) SRE/Ops: SLO targets, retention/observability impact, autoscaler constraints.
5) Security/Legal: any data residency, KMS, or audit requirements for Dedicated/Private.

Decision worksheet (one per feature + candidate packaging option)

- feature_name: <string>
- candidate_label: <string> (example: economy-quant, fidelity-plus)
- surfaces: Hosted | Dedicated | Private (list)
- default_model_variant: <string>
- slo_mapping: p50/p95 targets, availability target
- estimated_incremental_cost: "hosted: $X per-1M tokens; dedicated: Y GPU-hours/day"
- dev_ux: streaming: yes/no; tool-calling: yes/no; api_changes: brief summary
- observability_tier: standard | extended | premium
- security_gates: KMS required, PHI/PCI considerations
- rollout_constraints: canary_pct, tenant_requirements, rollout_windows

Evaluation rubric (score 0-5 each)

- fidelity_alignment (does it meet product fidelity needs)
- cost_efficiency (per-token economics)
- operational_risk (deployment/rollback risk)
- developer_ergonomics (API parity, migration difficulty)
- revenue_potential (commercial upside)

Example packaged options (illustrative table as text)

Option | Surfaces | SLOs p50/p95 | Cost delta (per-1M tokens) | Notes
--- | --- | --- | ---: | ---
Economy-quant | Hosted, Dedicated | 120ms / 450ms | +$120 | Quantized path, streaming disabled, optimized for high throughput.
Fidelity-plus | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | 45ms / 180ms | +$420 | Higher-memory variant, streaming enabled, premium telemetry.
Fallback-compat | Hosted only | 60ms / 350ms | +$240 | Compatibility chain and automatic fallback for legacy clients.

Required validation checks

1) Runtime benchmark: run canonical prompt set (>=50k tokens) and capture p50/p95, memory, GPU util, and batch distribution. Attach bench artifacts.
2) Cost simulation: run offline simulator across 3 traffic archetypes (interactive, bursty, high-volume batch) and capture per-tenant deltas.
3) Security signoff: confirm encryption, KMS integration, and retention policy for Dedicated/Private.
4) Telemetry plan: list telemetry events, derived KPIs, and dashboards/alerts necessary for rollback detection.

CLI examples

- Offline cost simulator
$ redwood-sim simulate --variant economy-quant --prompts prompts/high-volume-batch.json --output /tmp/econ-quant-report.json

- Containerized runtime benchmark
$ docker run --rm redwood/runtime-bench:latest --model quant-v1 --sequence 512 --batch 8 --duration 300s --report /out/bench.json

Minimum telemetry & KPIs

- Per-route latency (p50/p95/p99) by model variant
- Error rate (5xx + runtime failures) by tenant and route
- Token cost per successful request (derived metric)
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) and eviction counts if caching used
- Contention metrics: GPU utilization, batch queue length, backpressure events

Rollout playbook (step-by-step)

1) Developer preview (internal): enable behind feature flag for alpha tenants and collect 72h telemetry.
2) Canary: 3 enterprise tenants or 5% of eligible traffic, monitor KPIs hourly for 7 days.
3) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 14 days with automated health checks at each step.
4) Full launch: enable purchase/console mapping and SKU assignment. Publish customer-facing docs.
5) Post-launch review: 30-day impact review; decide iterate, repackage, or rollback.

Rollback criteria (automatic + manual)

Automatic triggers:
- p95 latency increases > 35% relative to baseline for >= 1 hour.
- Absolute error rate > 1.5% for >= 30 minutes.
- Per-tenant cost increase > 20% with no measurable fidelity improvement.

Manual triggers:
- Data residency or encryption non-compliance discovered.
- Repeated model-quality regressions flagged by eval harness.

Pricing & packaging heuristics

- Anchor packages around fidelity: "basic" (cost-sensitive), "balanced" (default), "premium" (high-fidelity + observability).
- Map per-token delta to micro-bundles (e.g., 50k token increments) and create additive SKU lines for fidelity add-ons.
- Dedicated "fidelity" packages should include a minimum 1-month reserved warm pool commitment.
- Private deployments: prefer metered billing with monthly reconciliation above negotiated caps.

Sample pricing mapping (illustrative)

Packaging | Suggested monthly add-on | Billing model
--- | ---: | ---
Economy-quant | $300 | Per-tenant bundle (adds 100M discounted tokens)
Fidelity-plus | $1,200 | Route/seat premium + per-token uplift
Observability-premium | $650 | Flat monthly + per-GB telemetry overage

Ownership and signoffs

- Product (feature lead): final packaging recommendation, PRD attachment, customer messaging.
- Pricing/Commercialization: SKU creation, contract language, revenue forecasting.
- Engineering (runtime): variant manifests, compatibility guarantees, benchmark artifacts.
- SRE/Ops: autoscaler config, SLO dashboards, alert thresholds.
- Security/Legal: compliance clauses, KMS and data-residency verification.

Packaging decision summary template (attach to PRD)

- feature: <name>
- chosen_package: <label>
- surfaces: <hosted/dedicated/private>
- expected_monthly_delta (example tenant): $<value>
- rollout_dates & canary_scope: <dates>
- acceptance_criteria: <KPIs and thresholds>
- owner_signoffs: Product / Pricing / Eng / SRE / Legal

Release note drafts

Internal (short):
"Feature <X> is available in Economy-quant and Fidelity-plus packaging. Economy-quant reduces per-token costs using a quantized runtime; Fidelity-plus preserves interactive latency with premium telemetry. See packaging playbook for rollout details."

External (customer-facing):
"Were launching two packaging options for Feature <X>: an economy package optimized for cost-sensitive workloads and a fidelity package that preserves interactive latency and advanced observability. Select package via Console or API during activation."

Appendix: canonical benchmark assets and dashboards

- canonical prompt sets: prompts/interactive-chat-typical.json, prompts/high-volume-batch.json
- suggested dashboards: per-route latency histogram, per-tenant cost burn & forecast, model fallback chain counts
